sections.h2: Where is the Onslow County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The counter is at 602 Anne Street in Jacksonville. Mail goes to a different spot, 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the main number is 910-347-3451.

Recordings are taken from 8 a.m. until 5:30 p.m. on weekdays. Marriage licenses stop at 5:15 p.m. Onslow is one of the few offices that stays open that late, which helps a seller whose closing runs long. The county also posted a delayed opening for the office on September 28, 2026, so a call before a long drive is a sensible habit.

  • Walk-in address: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville
  • Mailing address: 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville
  • Phone 910-347-3451, fax 910-347-3340
  • Weekday hours: 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

sections.h2: How far back do Onslow County real estate records go?
sections.html:
The office holds land records going back to 1734. Its Real Estate Records page lists conveyances, deeds of trust, cancellations of deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, separation agreements and road maintenance agreements.

Anything filed there is open to view at the counter. Staff will not complete forms or search a title for you. The county explains that doing so would amount to practicing law without a license, so owners who want a title check should hire a closing attorney or order one through a title company.

An owner can also ask in writing to have a Social Security, bank or card number blacked out of an image on the county website. The county charges nothing for that request.

sections.h2: What does Onslow County want on a deed before it is filed?
sections.html:
Three things stand out on the county's pages: an excise tax statement, a tax certification form and clean personal data. A deed missing any of them risks being returned.

  • Page one must show the excise tax, including a line for zero when nothing is due.
  • A tax-exempt transfer needs the legal reason for the exemption on page one.
  • A Tax Certification Form must be attached to the back of the original deed. That rule dates from July 1, 2013 and came from a decision of the Onslow County Tax Office.
  • Identity and account numbers stay out of the document unless the law or a court order requires them, or unless only the last four digits show.

Closing attorneys know these rules. A seller who prepares paperwork alone should phone 910-347-3451 first.

sections.h2: What does the Onslow County office charge, besides the state fees?
sections.html:
Beyond the state's uniform fees, Onslow County charges a few service amounts of its own, and it takes payment in specific forms.

Payment and filing rules on the Onslow County Recording Information page
ItemWhat the county page says
Extra instruments in one document$10 for each additional instrument
Credit cardsAccepted for $5 or more, with a 3% processing fee added
Business checksPhysical address and phone number required
Personal checksAddress, phone, and driver license number with issuing state
Vital recordsCash or money order only
Plats18 by 24 inches, mylar or paper

The base fee for a general instrument under G.S. 161-10 is $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page. A deed of trust or mortgage runs $64.00 for up to 35 pages. Satisfactions of deeds of trust carry no fee. The county links its latest fee schedule from the Recording Information page.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on an Onslow County house sale?
sections.html:
The seller does. The county page gives the tax as $1 for every $500, or any part of $500, of the consideration or value of the interest conveyed, and points readers to G.S. 105-228.

Collection happens at the register of deeds before the instrument is filed. A seller who forgets it will see the deed bounced. The office will not take a document that needs excise tax unless the amount is written on page one. Ask your closing attorney to total this tax with your payoff and any other seller charges so that your net sheet matches the check you receive.

sections.h2: Why does the filing time matter for an Onslow County sale?
sections.html:
Priority follows the clock. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, mortgage, option or lease of more than three years has no force against lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered where the land lies.

So a deed that sits in a desk drawer protects nobody. In Onslow County, a judgment filed against a seller on Monday can beat a buyer whose deed reaches the office on Tuesday. Ask the closing agent for the recording time and the book and page, and keep that confirmation with your sale papers. Sellers who accept a quick cash purchase should ask the same question and confirm that the lender's release has been recorded as well.

sections.h2: How do mail-in and plat recordings work in Onslow County?
sections.html:
Mail-ins need a self-addressed stamped envelope so the original can come back. Make checks payable to Onslow County Register of Deeds, for the exact total.

The office started taking plats from electronic vendors on May 1, 2021, and walk-in plat recording continues too. Statutory plat size is still 18 by 24 inches. Sticky notes stuck over wet-ink seals confuse the scanner, and a plat with sticky residue is rejected. If you are dividing a lot before a sale, plan for a clean original and a delivery by someone who knows the plat rules.

sections.h2: What do the census figures say about Onslow County?
sections.html:
Onslow County grew by 6.2% between the April 2020 base and July 2025, reaching 217,175 residents. It covers 762.08 square miles of land and holds 91,470 housing units.

Census survey data for 2020 to 2024 shows 75,265 households, a 63.7% owner-occupied rate and median gross rent of $1,265. The middle home value among owners is $236,400. About 25,185 residents are veterans. A house on a quiet street in Jacksonville and one far from town sell under different conditions, so use these county-wide figures only as background.

sections.h2: What should a seller do about liens before the deed goes in?
sections.html:
Clear them first. A lender's release of a deed of trust is filed at no charge, so the only cost is the lender's own timing.

Property tax attaches to the parcel as of the January listing date, which means an unpaid bill follows the house to the buyer's closing. Ask the Onslow County Tax Office for the balance owed and have it paid from your proceeds. A seller whose debts exceed the likely price should talk to a closing attorney before choosing a date, since a recorded lien blocks a clean transfer.

faqs.q: What is the street address of the Onslow County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 602 Anne Street, Jacksonville, NC. Mail is sent to 109 Old Bridge Street, Jacksonville, NC 28540, and the phone is 910-347-3451.

faqs.q: What time does the Onslow County Register of Deeds close?
faqs.a: Recording closes at 5:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The marriage license desk closes at 5:15 p.m.

faqs.q: Does Onslow County add a card fee when recording?
faqs.a: Yes. Credit cards are accepted for payments of $5 or more, and a 3% processing fee is added to the total.

faqs.q: Will the Onslow County office help me fill in a deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff cannot complete forms or run title searches, since they may not practice law. They can show you the public record.

faqs.q: What has to be attached to an Onslow County deed?
faqs.a: A Tax Certification Form goes on the back of the original deed. Page one must also show the excise tax amount, or the reason for any exemption.
